title: 471. The Road to The Great War: The Austrian Ultimatum (Part 3)

sentences.en: Coffee had just arrived when the French squadron was signaled.
sentences.zh: 法国舰队发出信号时，咖啡刚端上来。

sentences.en: The Tsar made me go up on the bridge with him.
sentences.zh: 沙皇让我和他一起上了舰桥。

sentences.en: It was a magnificent spectacle.
sentences.zh: 那是一场壮观的景象。

sentences.en: In a quivering silvery light, the France slowly surged forward over the turquoise and emerald waves, leaving a long white furrow behind her.
sentences.zh: 在颤动的银色光影中，法兰西号缓缓向前，划过绿松石色和翡翠色的波浪，身后留下一道长长的白色航迹。

sentences.en: Then she stopped majestically.
sentences.zh: 随后，它威严地停了下来。

sentences.en: The mighty warship which has brought the head of the French state is well worthy of her name.
sentences.zh: 这艘载着法国国家元首的强大战舰，确实无愧于它的名字。

sentences.en: She was indeed France, coming to Russia.
sentences.zh: 它确实是法兰西，来到了俄罗斯。

sentences.en: I felt my heart beating.
sentences.zh: 我感到心跳加速。

sentences.en: For a few minutes there was a prodigious din in the harbour.
sentences.zh: 几分钟内，港口里响起了巨大的轰鸣声。

sentences.en: The guns of the ships and the shore batteries firing, the crews cheering, the Marseillais answering the Russian national anthem, the cheers of thousands of spectators
sentences.zh: 舰船和岸上炮台的礼炮齐鸣，船员们欢呼雀跃，《马赛曲》与俄罗斯国歌交相辉映，成千上万名观众发出欢呼，

sentences.en: who had come from St. Petersburg on pleasure boats.
sentences.zh: 他们是乘坐游船从圣彼得堡赶来的。

sentences.en: At length, the President of the Republic, stepped on board the Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 最后，法兰西共和国总统登上了亚历山大号。

sentences.en: The Tsar received him at the gangway.
sentences.zh: 沙皇在舷梯旁迎接了他。

sentences.en: So those were the recollections of Maurice Palliologue, the improbably named French ambassador to St. Petersburg,
sentences.zh: 以上就是莫里斯·帕莱奥洛格的回忆，这位名字听起来有些不可思议的法国驻圣彼得堡大使，

sentences.en: who was remembering the arrival of the President of the French Republic,
sentences.zh: 他当时正在回忆法国共和国总统的到来，

sentences.en: President Poincaré, on the 20th of July, 1914.
sentences.zh: 也就是1914年7月20日到访的普恩加莱总统。

sentences.en: And Dominic, up front, we'll be coming to Monsieur Palliologue a bit later.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们稍后再谈帕莱奥洛格先生。

sentences.en: But just to say, this is a golden age for comical French ambassadors, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但不得不说，这真是个盛产滑稽法国大使的黄金时代，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，绝对是。

sentences.en: So there's the ambassador to St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是那位驻圣彼得堡的大使。

sentences.en: The one to London is even better, and we'll be coming to him in due course.
sentences.zh: 驻伦敦的那位更绝，我们稍后也会提到他。

sentences.en: For Combon.
sentences.zh: 为了康邦。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 没错，那真是太精彩了。

sentences.en: But this is, I mean, aside from the colour of the ambassador himself, I mean, this is a crucial moment in the story of the road to the outbreak of the First World War, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，撇开大使本人的色彩不谈，这可是第一次世界大战爆发前夕的关键时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you have the Tsar and the President of the French Republic, two heads of state, allied either side of Germany, the Western and the Eastern flank respectively,
sentences.zh: 因为沙皇和法国总统这两位国家元首，分别处于德国的东西两侧，结成了盟友，

sentences.en: meeting up in St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 他们在圣彼得堡会面了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And also, Tom, we ended last time with the Austrians preparing their ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 而且，汤姆，我们上次结束时提到奥地利人正在准备他们的最后通牒。

sentences.en: The Austrians have been writing their ultimatum, but they have not yet delivered it.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人一直在起草最后通牒，但尚未发出。

sentences.en: So they're waiting for the French to leave St. Petersburg before they will deliver it to Serbia.
sentences.zh: 他们正在等法国人离开圣彼得堡，然后才会将其递交给塞尔维亚。

sentences.en: So they are meeting in ignorance of what they suspect something may be coming, but they don't really know what it is.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是在不知情的情况下会面，虽然他们怀疑有什么事情要发生，但并不真正了解具体内容。

sentences.en: And so that makes this meeting all the more kind of pregnant with possibility.
sentences.zh: 这使得这次会面充满了各种可能性。

sentences.en: So last time, in the last couple of episodes, we talked about Austria and Germany.
sentences.zh: 上次，也就是过去几期节目中，我们谈到了奥地利和德国。

sentences.en: Let's turn our attention now to their great antagonist, and we'll start with Russia.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们把注意力转向他们的主要对手，先从俄罗斯开始。

sentences.en: So Russia, Tsarist Russia, is the world's largest country, country, 164 million people, huge, multi-ethnic, multi-cultural empire.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯，沙皇俄国，是世界上最大的国家，拥有1.64亿人口，是一个庞大的、多民族、多文化的帝国。

sentences.en: People compare it to the United States, don't they?
sentences.zh: 人们常把它和美国作比较，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That it's a continental empire.
sentences.zh: 因为它是一个大陆帝国。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And just as America is rising, people talk of the rise of Russia.
sentences.zh: 正如美国正在崛起一样，人们也在谈论俄罗斯的崛起。

sentences.en: That is exactly the right comparison.
sentences.zh: 这个比较非常恰当。

sentences.en: Those days, of course, Eastern Poland, Finland, Ukraine, they were all part of the Russian empire.
sentences.zh: 当然，在那个年代，波兰东部、芬兰、乌克兰，都是俄罗斯帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: At the head, since 1894, the autocrat of all the Russias,
sentences.zh: 自1894年以来，全俄国的独裁者就在其首位，

sentences.en: Nicholas II, of course, we all know what's going to happen to him in the Russian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉二世，当然，我们都知道他在俄国革命中会遭遇什么。

sentences.en: He's a very conservative man, family man, nervous, stubborn, not terribly bright.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常保守的人，顾家，神经质，固执，而且不太聪明。

sentences.en: Looks like George V.
sentences.zh: 长得像乔治五世。

sentences.en: Yeah, looks just like George V, but sort of slightly more Charles I in personality, I would say.
sentences.zh: 没错，长得和乔治五世一模一样，但我觉得性格上更像查理一世。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实。

sentences.en: And indeed fate.
sentences.zh: 而且确实是命运使然。

sentences.en: And in fate.
sentences.zh: 在命运面前。

sentences.en: And Russia has had a very tough beginning to the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯在20世纪初经历了一个非常艰难的开端。

sentences.en: They fought the Russo-Japanese War, in which they were utterly defeated.
sentences.zh: 他们打了日俄战争，结果惨败。

sentences.en: Then there was a little revolution.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一场小规模革命。

sentences.en: The Tsar had to call the Duma, a kind of parliament, which he didn't like doing.
sentences.zh: 沙皇不得不召集杜马，也就是一种议会，但他并不喜欢这样做。

sentences.en: And ever since then, Russia has turned away.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，俄罗斯就改变了方向。

sentences.en: So all through the 19th century, Russia expanding in Asia.
sentences.zh: 整个19世纪，俄罗斯一直在亚洲扩张。

sentences.en: And it's great rivalry with the British in Asia, the great game.
sentences.zh: 并与英国在亚洲展开了激烈的竞争，即“大博弈”。

sentences.en: But since the Russo-Japanese War, they've slightly turned back westward.
sentences.zh: 但自日俄战争以来，他们稍微转向了西方。

sentences.en: And their focus has been on their alliance with France, which they signed in 1894, and the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 他们的重心转向了1894年签署的法俄同盟，以及巴尔干地区。

sentences.en: And their eyes have been fixed on Southeast Europe.
sentences.zh: 他们的目光一直锁定在东南欧。

sentences.en: And really, the question is, why?
sentences.zh: 真正的问题是，为什么？

sentences.en: Because the Balkans are quite a long way from Russia.
sentences.zh: 因为巴尔干半岛离俄罗斯相当远。

sentences.en: Now, some people say, and you'll see this repeated often, it's because of their mystical pan-Slav solidarity.
sentences.zh: 有些人说，而且你会经常看到这种说法，是因为他们神秘的泛斯拉夫团结。

sentences.en: And orthodoxy.
sentences.zh: 还有东正教。

sentences.en: And orthodoxy, and all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 还有东正教，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And there's a bit of truth in that, but I think only a bit.
sentences.zh: 这其中有一点道理，但我认为只有一点点。

sentences.en: So it's the kind of thing that newspapers get very excited about.
sentences.zh: 这正是报纸会大肆渲染的那种话题。

sentences.en: In the same way, I think, as British newspapers right now are talking about our kith and kin beyond the seas.
sentences.zh: 就像我认为现在的英国报纸在谈论我们“海外的亲朋好友”一样。

sentences.en: You know, there's something slightly self-parodic, I think, about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得这有点自我讽刺的意味。

sentences.en: Except that in Australia and Canada, they really are kith and kin.
sentences.zh: 只不过在澳大利亚和加拿大，他们确实是亲朋好友。

sentences.en: Whereas the relationship between the Serbs and the Russians is much more loose.
sentences.zh: 而塞尔维亚人和俄罗斯人之间的关系则松散得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: Another thing that people often talk about is Russia is the third Rome.
sentences.zh: 人们经常谈论的另一件事是俄罗斯是“第三罗马”。

sentences.en: The second Rome is still standing, Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 第二罗马依然屹立不倒，那就是君士坦丁堡。

sentences.en: And it's part of a kind of decaying Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 它是衰落的奥斯曼帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, and there are quite a lot of Russian nationalists who think,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有很多俄罗斯民族主义者认为，

sentences.en: I'd love to have Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 我真想得到君士坦丁堡。

sentences.en: You know, imagine that commanding position.
sentences.zh: 你知道，想象一下那个战略要地。

sentences.en: But at the city of the Caesars, that would be a brilliant thing.
sentences.zh: 那是凯撒之城，那将是一件了不起的事情。

sentences.en: But also, it's the strategic position of Constantinople, that it's the kind of the chokehold of the Bosphorus
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是君士坦丁堡的战略位置，它是博斯普鲁斯海峡的咽喉，

sentences.en: that links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean and therefore to the world.
sentences.zh: 连接着黑海和地中海，进而通向世界。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the crucial thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那才是关键所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think that's the important thing, actually, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为那才是重点。

sentences.en: And it's not whether or not they actually control Constantinople itself.
sentences.zh: 这并不在于他们是否真正控制了君士坦丁堡本身。

sentences.en: It's whether they control the straits that lead from the Black Sea into the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 而在于他们是否控制了从黑海通往地中海的海峡。

sentences.en: Because in a nice sort of nod to events in the 2020s,
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，这与2020年代发生的事件遥相呼应，

sentences.en: Russia's economy depends upon Ukrainian grain exports.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯的经济依赖于乌克兰的粮食出口。

sentences.en: And the control of those straits is crucial to get those grain ships out of the Black Sea and into the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 控制这些海峡对于让运粮船驶出黑海进入地中海至关重要。

sentences.en: And if the straits are closed off, then Russia's economy is in terrible trouble.
sentences.zh: 如果海峡被封锁，俄罗斯的经济就会陷入巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: And the Balkans are the hinterland to the straits.
sentences.zh: 而巴尔干半岛正是这些海峡的腹地。

sentences.en: So it's very important, as the Russians see it, that no enemy power controls that hinterland and therefore, by extension, the straits themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以，在俄罗斯人看来，绝不能让敌对势力控制这片腹地，进而控制海峡本身，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: Because they could hold the Russians to ransom over the grain exports and they could stop the Russian Black Sea fleet getting into the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 因为他们可以利用粮食出口要挟俄罗斯，并阻止俄罗斯黑海舰队进入地中海。

sentences.en: And so it's a problem for the Russians, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这对俄罗斯人来说是个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: That the Balkans are kind of in a mess.
sentences.zh: 巴尔干半岛乱成了一锅粥。

sentences.en: So Ottoman power has collapsed.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼帝国的势力已经崩溃了。

sentences.en: We've been talking about this in our previous episodes about the assassination of the Archduke.
sentences.zh: 我们在之前关于大公遇刺的节目中讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: And you have all these kind of nationalist seething resentments bubbling away.
sentences.zh: 所有这些民族主义的怨恨都在暗流涌动。

sentences.en: And I suppose you could either say, well, that's a real problem, or you could say, you know, it's a good place to fish.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以说，这真是一个大问题，或者也可以说，这是一个浑水摸鱼的好地方。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: I think it's both.
sentences.zh: 我认为两者皆有。

sentences.en: So I think their fear for them is if the Austrians get hegemony in the Balkans or some other power.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们担心的是，如果奥地利人或其他势力在巴尔干半岛获得霸权。

sentences.en: But the opportunity is, I mean, they had backed Bulgaria.
sentences.zh: 但机会在于，我的意思是，他们曾经支持过保加利亚。

sentences.en: Now they've switched horses and they're backing Serbia.
sentences.zh: 现在他们换了立场，开始支持塞尔维亚。

sentences.en: Serbia, as we said, has doubled in size since the Balkan Wars.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，塞尔维亚在巴尔干战争后领土扩大了一倍。

sentences.en: So the Russians, you know, Serbia is their client.
sentences.zh: 所以俄罗斯人，你知道，塞尔维亚是他们的附庸。

sentences.en: It hasn't all been plain sailing though, because the Russians have twice, as they see it, had to give ground in the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 但这并非一帆风顺，因为在俄罗斯人看来，他们已经在巴尔干半岛两次被迫让步。

sentences.en: Once when Austria annexed Bosnia and the Serbs are very cross about it, but the Serbs and the Russians backed down.
sentences.zh: 一次是奥地利吞并波斯尼亚时，塞尔维亚人非常愤怒，但塞尔维亚和俄罗斯选择了退让。

sentences.en: And again, during the Balkan Wars, there had been a great hullabaloo about whether or not Serbia was going to get Albania and access to the Adriatic.
sentences.zh: 另一次是在巴尔干战争期间，关于塞尔维亚是否能获得阿尔巴尼亚和亚得里亚海出海口的问题，曾闹得沸沸扬扬。

sentences.en: The Russians and Austrians had been slightly at daggers drawn about it.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯和奥地利曾为此剑拔弩张。

sentences.en: And again, Serbia and Russia had backed down.
sentences.zh: 结果塞尔维亚和俄罗斯再次退让了。

sentences.en: So the two sides there had drawn different lessons.
sentences.zh: 所以双方从中吸取了不同的教训。

sentences.en: The Austrians said, hey, listen, Serbs and the Russians were always backed down.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人说，嘿，听着，塞尔维亚人和俄罗斯人总是会退让的。

sentences.en: And the Russians said, we've done it twice.
sentences.zh: 而俄罗斯人说，我们已经退让过两次了。

sentences.en: Yeah, never again.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝不再有下一次。

sentences.en: And we can't afford to do it again.
sentences.zh: 我们再也承受不起了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that is a big problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个大问题。

sentences.en: And the other thing, of course, is that Russia is in a different place in 1914 than it was before then.
sentences.zh: 当然，另一件事是，1914年的俄罗斯与之前相比处于不同的境地。

sentences.en: Because as we said in the last episode, Russia has been modernizing very faSt.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们在上一集所说，俄罗斯一直在快速现代化。

sentences.en: It has been spending huge amounts of money training its men on armaments and, above all, on its railways.
sentences.zh: 它投入了巨额资金用于训练士兵、购买军备，最重要的是，用于铁路建设。

sentences.en: So their army is now the biggest in the world.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的军队现在是世界上规模最大的。

sentences.en: It's going to be 2 million people by the end of the 1910s, bigger than Germany and Austria put together.
sentences.zh: 到1910年代末，人数将达到200万，比德国和奥地利加起来还要多。

sentences.en: They are feeling much more self-confident than they were even 10 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 他们比10年前更加自信了。

sentences.en: But there is another thing, actually.
sentences.zh: 但实际上还有另一件事。

sentences.en: The guy called Dominic Leven has a book called Towards the Flame about Russia and the origins of the First World, which is a brilliant book if people are interested in Russia.
sentences.zh: 有个叫多米尼克·利文的人写了一本书叫《走向火焰》，讲述了俄罗斯与第一次世界大战的起源，如果人们对俄罗斯感兴趣，这是一本非常棒的书。

sentences.en: The Russians, like the Austrians and like the Germans, have this sort of ticking clock at the back of their heads.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人，像奥地利人和德国人一样，脑后都有一个倒计时钟。

sentences.en: So in their case, the ticking clock is they are frightened, not that the Ottoman Empire will fall apart, but the Ottoman Empire will actually stage a bit of a comeback.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这个倒计时钟是他们担心的不是奥斯曼帝国会崩溃，而是奥斯曼帝国实际上会卷土重来。

sentences.en: The Ottomans have just ordered two dreadnoughts from a British firm, Armstrong and Vickers, and they've got five more to come further down the line.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼人刚刚向一家英国公司——阿姆斯特朗和维克斯公司——订购了两艘无畏舰，未来还有五艘在排队。

sentences.en: And do the Russians have any dreadnoughts in the Black Sea?
sentences.zh: 那么俄罗斯人在黑海有无畏舰吗？

sentences.en: They do not.
sentences.zh: 他们没有。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So when all those Ottoman ships arrive, the Russians will be outnumbered in the Black Sea six to one.
sentences.zh: 所以当所有这些奥斯曼战舰抵达时，俄罗斯人在黑海的兵力将以一比六处于劣势。

sentences.en: And their foreign minister, a guy called Sergei Sazanov, says to his colleagues, this will be absolutely calamitous for our ambitions.
sentences.zh: 他们的外交大臣，一个叫谢尔盖·萨佐诺夫的人，对同事们说，这对我们的野心来说将是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: We cannot, he says, stand by and watch the expansion of the Ottoman Navy, because that will torpedo forever our chance of getting a hold,
sentences.zh: 他说，我们不能袖手旁观，看着奥斯曼海军扩张，因为那将永远摧毁我们获得控制权的机会，

sentences.en: getting control of the straits on which our economy depends.
sentences.zh: 获得对我们经济所依赖的海峡的控制权。

sentences.en: And the Ottomans could close the straits.
sentences.zh: 而且奥斯曼人可能会封锁海峡。

sentences.en: They could close the straits, exactly.

sentences.zh: 德国人和奥地利人都是可怕的家伙。

sentences.en: We should take a hard line because the only line they understand, you stand up to a bully, you know, and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们应该采取强硬路线，因为这是他们唯一能听懂的路线，你要对抗恶霸，你知道，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: So Sazenov has confirmed he's been encouraged in his existing assumption, which is a hard line is the only possible line to take.
sentences.zh: 于是萨佐诺夫确认他现有的假设得到了鼓励，那就是强硬路线是唯一可行的路线。

sentences.en: And so that afternoon, he goes to an absolutely vital and crucial meeting of the Council of
sentences.zh: 那天下午，他去参加了一个绝对至关重要、决定性的会议，那是俄罗斯的

sentences.en: Ministers in Russia.
sentences.zh: 部长会议。

sentences.en: And he says, listen, guys, we have appeased the Austrians and the Germans for too long.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，伙计们，我们对奥地利人和德国人的绥靖政策已经太久了。

sentences.en: We have a historic mission in the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 我们在巴尔干半岛有着历史使命。

sentences.en: And if we back down now, we will lose all our prestige, all our authority forever.
sentences.zh: 如果我们现在退缩，我们将永远失去所有的威望和权威。

sentences.en: We will no longer be a great power.
sentences.zh: 我们将不再是一个大国。

sentences.en: Which is exactly what the Austrians are saying.
sentences.zh: 这正是奥地利人所说的。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Both of them are saying exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 他们俩说的完全一样。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: This defensive aggression.
sentences.zh: 这种防御性的侵略。

sentences.en: So the question for me, actually, that has often puzzled me about this story is I always understood why the Austrians cared.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这个故事中一直让我困惑的问题是，我一直理解为什么奥地利人会在意。

sentences.en: I mean, it's their heir that's been murdered and they think it's their integrity of their empire that's at stake.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，被谋杀的是他们的继承人，他们认为这关乎帝国的完整性。

sentences.en: What had always puzzled me was why the Russians cared.
sentences.zh: 一直让我困惑的是为什么俄罗斯人会在意。

sentences.en: I mean, Serbia is a long way from Russia.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，塞尔维亚离俄罗斯很远。

sentences.en: And actually, it was only in the last few weeks while kind of reading about this that I kind of finally understood.
sentences.zh: 实际上，就在过去几周阅读相关资料时，我才终于明白。

sentences.en: The Russians care a lot about the straits and access to the straits because it's really, really important for them diplomatically and economically.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人非常关心海峡以及通往海峡的通道，因为这对他们的外交和经济来说真的非常非常重要。

sentences.en: They care a bit, I suppose, about Slav brotherhood and that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 我想，他们对斯拉夫兄弟情谊之类的东西也有一点关心。

sentences.en: Yeah, orthodoxy and all that.
sentences.zh: 是的，东正教之类的。

sentences.en: But the key thing is, from their perspective, they have backed down twice already in the last five or six years in the Balkans over Bosnia, the annexation of Bosnia, and then
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，从他们的角度来看，在过去五六年里，他们在巴尔干半岛已经退缩了两次，一次是波斯尼亚，即波斯尼亚的吞并，然后是

sentences.en: in the Balkan Wars about whether or not Serbia would be allowed to occupy Albania.
sentences.zh: 在巴尔干战争中，关于是否允许塞尔维亚占领阿尔巴尼亚的问题。

sentences.en: And as they see it, the Austrians are just asking too much to ask them to back down three times in five years.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，奥地利人要求他们在五年内退缩三次，这要求实在太过分了。

sentences.en: So although I personally can completely understand why the Austrians acted as they did, it has to be said they are making a hell of an ask, as it were.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然我个人完全能理解奥地利人为什么那样做，但不得不说，他们提出的要求简直是强人所难。

sentences.en: A big ask.
sentences.zh: 一个巨大的要求。

sentences.en: A big ask.
sentences.zh: 一个巨大的要求。

sentences.en: It's a very big ask.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大的要求。

sentences.en: It's basically saying to the Russians, yet again, you must concede to us on this.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是在对俄罗斯人说，再一次，你们必须在这件事上向我们让步。

sentences.en: And at a time when the Russians are worried about the Ottomans getting all their dreadnoughts.
sentences.zh: 而且是在俄罗斯人担心奥斯曼人获得所有无畏舰的时候。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And will they be able to keep the straits open and all that kind of thing?
sentences.zh: 他们还能保持海峡畅通吗，诸如此类的事情？

sentences.en: Now, you might think, come on, can the two of them get together and sort this out?
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会想，得了吧，他们俩就不能坐下来解决这个问题吗？

sentences.en: But you made this point, I think, Tom, in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，你在上一集里提到了这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They don't have email.
sentences.zh: 他们没有电子邮件。

sentences.en: They can't talk on the phone.
sentences.zh: 他们不能打电话。

sentences.en: Everything has to be done through intermediaries like Maurice Palliog.
sentences.zh: 一切都必须通过像莫里斯·帕莱奥洛格这样的中间人来完成。

sentences.en: And he's just making stuff up.
sentences.zh: 而他只是在编造事实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Ambassadors.
sentences.zh: 大使们。

sentences.en: Ambassadors who will put their own spin on things.
sentences.zh: 大使们会按照自己的意愿去解读事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are allies, there's real Chinese whispers.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们是盟友，这简直就是传声筒游戏。

sentences.en: It's hard for them actually to get together and talk about it, even if they wanted to.
sentences.zh: 即使他们想，他们也很难真正坐下来谈论这件事。

sentences.en: And both sides think, time is running out, we are embattled, the others are malevolent and plotting against us.
sentences.zh: 双方都认为，时间不多了，我们四面楚歌，对方心怀恶意，正在密谋反对我们。

sentences.en: Because the Russians actually overestimate Austrian military prowess, don't they?
sentences.zh: 因为俄罗斯人实际上高估了奥地利的军事实力，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I think the Austrians overate Austrian military prowess.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我认为奥地利人自己也高估了奥地利的军事实力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But the Russians, I mean, the Russians, even though they have these massive forces and are relatively confident, they're still, you know, they don't want to be caught out.
sentences.zh: 但俄罗斯人，我的意思是，尽管俄罗斯人拥有庞大的军队并且相对自信，但他们仍然，你知道，他们不想被抓个正着。

sentences.en: They don't want to have a mobilizing empire on their doorstep.
sentences.zh: 他们不想在家门口面对一个正在动员的帝国。

sentences.en: Do you know, Tom, I was thinking about this in the break between recording these two episodes that we've recorded this morning.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，汤姆，在今天早上录制的这两集节目之间的休息时间里，我一直在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: I was thinking about what made this different from Napoleonic Wars or something.
sentences.zh: 我在想是什么让这次战争与拿破仑战争或其他战争不同。

sentences.en: And I guess part of it is that you can make a mistake and embark on, you know, the nine years war or the seven years war or something.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因是，你可能会犯错并卷入，你知道，九年战争或七年战争之类的。

sentences.en: And, you know, what's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: You'll lose Menorca.
sentences.zh: 你会失去梅诺卡岛。

sentences.en: The results will not necessarily be apocalyptic for you if it goes against you.
sentences.zh: 如果结果对你不利，也不一定会导致世界末日。

sentences.en: But one reason that they are all so frightened, I think, is because they know with industrialized total warfare, the stakes are so high.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们都如此害怕的一个原因是，他们知道在工业化的全面战争中，赌注太高了。

sentences.en: And if you get this wrong, it's not, you know, you'll lose a couple of provinces.
sentences.zh: 如果你搞砸了，这不仅仅是，你知道，失去几个省份的问题。

sentences.en: If you get this wrong, you could lose everything.
sentences.zh: 如果你搞砸了，你可能会失去一切。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Your society could cease to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 你的社会可能会不复存在。

sentences.en: And I think that heightens the sense of urgency for them.
sentences.zh: 我认为这加剧了他们的紧迫感。

sentences.en: You cannot allow your opponents to get a head start.
sentences.zh: 你不能让你的对手抢占先机。

sentences.en: And so it's obvious that Austria is going to have to mobilize if it's going to have a crack at Serbia.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，如果奥地利想对塞尔维亚动手，它就必须动员起来。

sentences.en: And Austria is a hostile power on your doorstep if you're Russian.
sentences.zh: 如果你是俄罗斯人，奥地利就是一个在你家门口的敌对势力。

sentences.en: So that then implies, well, we'd better start thinking about mobilization.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着，好吧，我们最好开始考虑动员了。

sentences.en: Especially because you are slow.
sentences.zh: 尤其是因为你们动作很慢。

sentences.en: If you're Russian, you are slow.
sentences.zh: 如果你是俄罗斯人，你们很慢。

sentences.en: You have the vast army.
sentences.zh: 你们拥有庞大的军队。

sentences.en: You have vast territory.
sentences.zh: 你们拥有广阔的领土。

sentences.en: You have to bring in people from a long distance.
sentences.zh: 你们必须从很远的地方调集人员。

sentences.en: So that night, the 24th, 25th, they've sent a message to Serbia via the Serbian ambassador.
sentences.zh: 所以那天晚上，24日到25日，他们通过塞尔维亚大使向塞尔维亚发出了信息。

sentences.en: They've said, you can't accept this ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你们不能接受这个最后通牒。

sentences.en: That would be to commit suicide.
sentences.zh: 那等于是自杀。

sentences.en: You know, we will stand by you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们会支持你们。

sentences.en: They've almost effectively given the Serbians a blank check of their own.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上几乎给了塞尔维亚一张他们自己的空白支票。

sentences.en: You stand firm and we'll sort this out for you.
sentences.zh: 你们立场坚定，我们会为你们解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So the Serbians have their decision to make.
sentences.zh: 所以塞尔维亚人必须做出决定。

sentences.en: The French are off at sea.
sentences.zh: 法国人正在海上。

sentences.en: But as you say, Tom, the big thing for the Russians is, do we get moving?
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，汤姆，对俄罗斯人来说，最重要的事情是，我们要行动起来吗？

sentences.en: Because we have to get cracking.
sentences.zh: 因为我们必须抓紧时间。

sentences.en: If this is going to go horribly wrong, we can't mess around.
sentences.zh: 如果事情要变得一团糟，我们就不能乱来。

sentences.en: So dawn breaks on the 25th of July.
sentences.zh: 7月25日的黎明破晓了。

sentences.en: And of course, it's not a minor point.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并非小事。

sentences.en: The Russians are deciding before everybody.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人比所有人都先做出决定。

sentences.en: I mean, they're literally up before everybody else because of the time difference.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，由于时差，他们确实比其他人起得早。

sentences.en: So on Saturday, the 25th of July, they know that that evening, the decision will have been made because the Serbians will have probably rejected the ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 所以7月25日星期六，他们知道那天晚上决定就会做出，因为塞尔维亚人很可能已经拒绝了最后通牒。

sentences.en: And so they meet in a place called Krasnoye Selo, which is outside the capital.
sentences.zh: 于是他们在首都外一个叫克拉斯诺耶塞洛的地方会面。

sentences.en: It's like one of the Tsar's summer palaces.
sentences.zh: 那就像是沙皇的夏宫之一。

sentences.en: He is there, Nicholas II.
sentences.zh: 他在那里，尼古拉二世。

sentences.en: He's in a very fancy kind of white uniform of the guards, the Tsars.
sentences.zh: 他穿着那种非常华丽的沙皇卫队白色制服。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful day.
sentences.zh: 那是一个美好的日子。

sentences.en: It is that classic kind of a Viennese waltz.
sentences.zh: 那是一种经典的维也纳华尔兹氛围。

sentences.en: Piano in the back.
sentences.zh: 背景里有钢琴声。

sentences.en: The French windows are open to the garden and they're a very incongruous scene.
sentences.zh: 法式落地窗通向花园，这是一个非常不协调的场景。

sentences.en: And he's sitting around with his ministers.
sentences.zh: 他正和他的部长们坐在一起。

sentences.en: And Sazonov says, guys, we need to start mobilizing our troops now.
sentences.zh: 萨佐诺夫说，伙计们，我们需要现在就开始动员我们的军队。

sentences.en: That will make an impression on Austria-Hungary.
sentences.zh: 那会对奥匈帝国产生影响。

sentences.en: And what we'll do is we will mobilize just a bit of them.
sentences.zh: 我们要做的只是动员其中一部分。

sentences.en: So the four Western military districts, that is Moscow, Kiev, Kazan, Odessa.
sentences.zh: 也就是四个西部军区，即莫斯科、基辅、喀山、敖德萨。

sentences.en: So we will mobilize those.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将动员这些地区。

sentences.en: We'll cancel leave, reservists back to the training camps, put the railways on alert, all of this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们将取消休假，让预备役人员回到训练营，让铁路进入警戒状态，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: It's not full general mobilization and it's not a declaration of war or anything like it, but it's just getting stuff going.
sentences.zh: 这不是全面的总动员，也不是宣战或类似的事情，只是让事情运转起来。

sentences.en: Just a defensive measure.
sentences.zh: 只是一种防御措施。

sentences.en: It's a defensive measure, but also that will show the Austrians that we are serious.
sentences.zh: 这是一种防御措施，但也会向奥地利人表明我们是认真的。

sentences.en: And that will mean that the Austrians say, okay, enough.
sentences.zh: 这意味着奥地利人会说，好吧，够了。

sentences.en: We've gone too far.
sentences.zh: 我们走得太远了。

sentences.en: We will back down.
sentences.zh: 我们会退缩的。

sentences.en: Of course, this is an absolutely crucial point in the story because at this moment, somebody is going to have to back down a long way.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是故事中绝对关键的一点，因为在这一刻，有人将不得不做出巨大的让步。

sentences.en: Either the Russians will have to call off their mobilization and send everybody back home again,
sentences.zh: 要么俄罗斯人必须取消动员并让所有人回家，

sentences.en: or the Austrians will have to not go through with the ultimatum that they have long prepared.
sentences.zh: 要么奥地利人必须放弃他们早已准备好的最后通牒。

sentences.en: So the stakes are suddenly very, very high now.
sentences.zh: 所以现在赌注突然变得非常非常高了。

sentences.en: And a Russian mobilization also has knock-on effects for Germany.
sentences.zh: 而且俄罗斯的动员对德国也有连锁反应。

sentences.en: It does indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Because what are the Germans going to do?
sentences.zh: 因为德国人会怎么做呢？

sentences.en: And all the time, the clock is ticking because at six o'clock this afternoon,
sentences.zh: 而且一直以来，时钟都在滴答作响，因为今天下午六点，

sentences.en: Saturday, the 25th of July, the Serbs will have to give their answer to the Austrian ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 7月25日星期六，塞尔维亚人必须对奥地利的最后通牒给出答复。

sentences.en: And as it happens, there are now just seven days left before the world war begins.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，距离世界大战爆发现在只剩下七天了。

sentences.en: Goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Storm clouds.
sentences.zh: 乌云密布。

sentences.en: All of that.
sentences.zh: 就是那样。

sentences.en: So in our next episode, we will follow the course of those seven days that leads to apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 所以在下一集中，我们将追踪导致世界末日的那七天的进程。

sentences.en: And patriotic listeners will be delighted to know that in our next episode, Britain will enter the story.
sentences.zh: 爱国听众会很高兴地知道，在我们的下一集中，英国将进入这个故事。

sentences.en: So if you're not a member of the Rest is History Club, you'll be getting that in due course.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不是“历史余韵”俱乐部的成员，你到时候会看到的。

sentences.en: If you are, you can get that straight away.
sentences.zh: 如果你是，你可以立即收听。

sentences.en: And if you would like to join the club and get immediate access, you can go to therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 如果你想加入俱乐部并获得即时访问权限，你可以访问 therestishistory.com。

sentences.en: But until then, à bientôt.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
